correctness.rationale: An exact bijective lattice count proves \(D(G)=p\). For every other residue the first two bands give \(p+j-\delta\); if \(\delta>0\), the third band compensates by \(R_2\ge\delta-j+1\), since \(d-\lceil dv/a\rceil=\lfloor d(a-v)/a\rfloor\le\lfloor(a-v-1)/2\rfloor\). The condition \(d\le(a-1)/2\) supplies this inequality. The last successor \(G+a\) also gains a representation and translation by \(a\) covers all greater numbers. Bounds include \(a=3\) and every endpoint. The packaged checker verifies 30,750 parameter triples, 1,940,622 residue successor checks and 291,790 independent DP comparisons; finite checks supplement, not replace, proof.

value.rationale: The motivating source identifies difficulty after \(p=\lfloor a/2\rfloor\). The finding gives a uniform closed form across an interval containing \(h+d+1\) distinct representation thresholds for each admissible odd \(a\) and difference \(d\), not just isolated values. Its slope changes from \(a+2d\) to \(a\). The three-band saturation inequality explains the regime; outside the range \(d\le h\), even \((a,d,p)=(5,3,8)\) has actual \(g_p=74\) rather than the extrapolated \(72\). No claim to all \(p\) or the genus is made.
